newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Electric Company relies on ING bank credit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Electric Company relies on ING bank credit.

text.p: Bulgaria's debt-ridden National Electricity Company (NEC) plans to borrow $4 million from ING Bank, part of Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, a senior official said on Tuesday.
"We will sign an agreement with the ING Bank on Wednesday if its last version complies with our latest negotiations," NEC's financial director Krasimir Kanev told Reuters.
The NEC is among 70 indebted state companies due to be isolated from credits while they are restructured under a government austerity programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Bulgaria's central bank barred local trade banks from granting credits to the NEC last month in line with the commitments made to the IMF.

ING opened its Bulgarian branch in 1994, aiming to focus on corporate banking and to facilitate payments and transfers, trade treasury products on global markets and provide import and export financing.
"We need the loan urgently to pay for equipment supplies and part of the summer repairs of coal-fired power plants," Kanev said.
"If we have some money left, we will also buy coal for the thermal power plant in Varna."

The Varna plant, which did not run last winter due to a lack of funds for coal, is supposed to replace the electricity production of the oldest 440-megawatt nuclear reactor at Kozloduy, closed for safety tests amid international concern.

In July the European Union said it would grant 10 million Ecus to Bulgaria's energy sector as compensation for closing the controversial reactor and buying coal for the Varna plant for the coming winter for half of this amount.
"We hope to receive the money in October and then we will buy some more coal for the Varna plant," Kanev said.

Bulgaria, currently in the throes of an economic crisis, imports some 80 percent of its energy resources and the six Kozloduy reactors, which total 3,760 megawatts, produced more than half of the country's electricity.
